gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-thaana: Flat, stencil-cut strokes of single weight and tightly packed letters give Bevellier its look. Noto Sans Thaana, a sans-serif with wide channels into each counter, loosens everything the heading packs tight.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-tirhuta: Flat, stencil-cut and tightly spaced, Bevellier looks cut from card. Noto Sans Tirhuta, a sans with cut-back terminals and a dominant x-height, spreads out beside those tight lines and lets the heading stay the loud one.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-ugaritic: Bevellier draws every line as if traced with one marker tip, flat and tightly spaced. Noto Sans Ugaritic keeps its lowercase close to cap height with open mouths, so paragraphs read softly and without fuss.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-vai: Ribbon-cut strokes of constant width define Bevellier. Bevellier is best at being looked at, while Noto Sans Vai, a sans-serif with solid word shapes, is best at being read.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-wancho: Wire-bent strokes of constant thickness and tight spacing make Bevellier look like a sign. And Noto Sans Wancho, hulking and chalky with wide-gapped e terminals, pushes back with real bulk.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-numans: Tight, flat, stencil-cut: that is Bevellier, every stroke ending at one measured thickness. Numans, with its swollen, widely tracked lowercase and far-hanging s ends, feels loose and plump next to that crowded heading.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-oxygen: Thread-stitched strokes, tightly packed: that's Bevellier. Bevellier does best as a showpiece, while Oxygen, a sans-serif with open curves and lowercase close to capital height, does best at carrying text.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-radio-canada: Flat stencil cuts, tightly spaced: that is Bevellier. Radio Canada, a sans-serif with tall, full c, s and z, reads steadily over many lines, with a clear opening at the end of each curve.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-roboto: Roboto brings generous round mouths and lowercase close to capital height, a sans that keeps quiet beside Bevellier. Paragraphs of it flow steadily, with none of the heading's stencil fuss.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-ruda: Bevellier is flat, stencil-cut and set very tight, with squat ascenders. Ruda, a sans-serif with a sizable x-height and wire-like monoline strokes, makes paragraphs feel easy to settle into.
